title: kickoff can be meta+rightclicked beyond its usual constraints
line: After resizing Kickoff (or any panel popup) with Meta+right-drag, it snaps back next to its launcher instead of staying detached in the middle of the screen.
explanation: Applet popups keep themselves next to their applet by sending KWin a new position whenever their size changes. KWin ignores those position requests while a window is being interactively moved or resized, and never applied them afterwards, so a Meta+right-drag from the popup's left edge moved that edge and left the popup floating away from the launcher until it was closed. The change applies the popup's last requested position again when the interactive resize ends.

commits.message:
xdgshellwindow: re-place applet popups after an interactive resize

Position requests from applet popups are ignored while they're being
moved or resized, so a Meta+right-drag from the anchored edge left the
popup detached from its applet; apply the last requested position again.

BUG: 520409

media.caption: Pure master: after Meta+right-dragging the right edge out and then the left edge in, Kickoff floats detached from the launcher.
With the fix: the same drags leave Kickoff next to the launcher.
Pure master: the left-edge drag pulls Kickoff away from the launcher and it stays there.
With the fix: the popup still follows the drag, then snaps back to the launcher on release.

review.text: Re-applying the applet popup's last requested PlasmaShellSurface position after an interactive resize is a reasonable way to prevent Kickoff from staying detached after Meta+right-drag, though the popup still detaches visually mid-drag before snapping back. However, the new signal connection in `XdgToplevelWindow::installPlasmaShellSurface` introduces a use-after-free hazard and can fire on a deleted window during teardown.
changes: Fix the dangling `shellSurface` pointer lifetime bug: the connection uses `this` as both sender and receiver while capturing raw `shellSurface` (directly and via `updatePosition`), so if the client destroys `org_kde_plasma_surface` before `xdg_toplevel`, `interactiveMoveResizeFinished` dereferences a freed pointer. Use `shellSurface` as the receiver/context object (or guard via `QPointer` `m_plasmaShellSurface`) and ensure it is disconnected in `handleRoleDestroyed()`.

Guard against running `updatePosition()` on a deleted window: `XdgSurfaceWindow::destroyWindow()` calls `handleRoleDestroyed()` and `markAsDeleted()` before emitting `interactiveMoveResizeFinished()` if a popup closes mid-resize, so check `!isDeleted()` (or disconnect in `handleRoleDestroyed()`).

Consider adding a KWin autotest covering interactive resize of an `AppletPopup` window (and verify whether refusing compositor Meta+right-drag on anchored edges is preferable to snapping back on release).

reviews.text: Correct diagnosis in the right repo: XdgToplevelWindow's updatePosition drops plasma-shell position requests while isInteractiveMoveResize(), and nothing reapplies them, so a Meta+right-drag from the anchored edge leaves the applet popup stranded. Reapplying the last requested position on interactiveMoveResizeFinished (applet popups with a set position only) is small, also resets the gravities, and leaves normal windows untouched. The after video shows the popup following the drag and returning next to the launcher on release, which matches the reporter's expected result (the reporter already describes the detachment during the drag as temporary). Nit: the popup still visibly detaches while dragging and then jumps back; worth a sentence in the MR text.
